_meta.purpose: Machine-readable claims about NEXUS's real behavior, each paired with the exact command that provides evidence for it. This file is human-authored and checked into git — NOT generated by NEXUS itself. A system writing and grading its own verification claims would be circular; the manifest has to originate outside the thing it verifies, the same reason RAID's approval gate can't be self-approved.
_meta.honestDistinction: Every entry separates 'rawCheck' (what the command literally measures — a test pass count, a real HTTP response) from 'claim' (the human interpretation of what that evidence supports). A passing rawCheck is evidence FOR the claim, not identical to it. The runner (scripts/run-verification-manifest.cjs) never conflates the two in its output.

claims.claim: The core system's real test suite passes.
LOOM's declaration schema (component/seam/hook/wire/concern) is structurally sound, including the concern kind added 2026-07-14.
LOOM can generate a real, working sovereign system (CLI+API+registration+contract) from one operations list, including correct :param routing and POST body handling.
RAID's approval gate correctly distinguishes allowed, denied, and proof-required sources and actions.
Guardian will not dispatch real browser-control commands (navigate/DOM-mutate/driver-exec) from an unauthorized source — this is enforced code, not just a documented intention.
claims.rawCheck: raid._approveTool('some-random-source', ..., {action:'browser'}) returns approved:false; raid._approveTool('copilot', ..., {action:'browser'}) returns approved:true
claims.command: node -e "const raid=require('./cortex/core/raid/index.js'); const a=raid._approveTool('some-random-source','x',{action:'browser'}); const b=raid._approveTool('copilot','x',{action:'browser'}); if(a.approved) throw new Error('unauthorized source was approved'); if(!b.approved) throw new Error('copilot was wrongly denied'); console.log('PASS');"

claims.claim: forge routes all LLM calls through Guardian/RAID and never hardcodes a specific external provider.
